title: Digital Technology Student Workers - Software Engineering
description_md:
**Job Description**

This autumn semester, we are excited to welcome **four** new student workers to join our teams in Billund. These roles span across front-end and full-stack software engineering, offering great opportunities to learn, grow, and make an impact.

**Student Worker, BrickLink Technology (role 1)**

As our Student Worker – Frontend Development, you'll build real frontend features on BrickLink.com alongside engineers who are rebuilding the platform on a modern stack. You'll join a product team with engineering, product, and design partners, and your work will reach a live global audience. You'll experience both a long-running production system and a greenfield modern architecture while contributing to member-facing experiences across home pages, accounts, sessions, and community touchpoints within the LEGO® ecosystem.

**Required Qualifications**

* JavaScript or TypeScript fundamentals

* Experience with/exposure to React (or a comparable component framework)

* Experience with/exposure to HTML and CSS - semantic markup, responsive layout

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience with/exposure to Next.js or a modern SSR framework

* Basic experience with backend/APIs or testing

**What you'll build**

* Frontend features that improve the experience for BrickLink members.

* Pages aligned with LEGO design and component systems.

* Solutions that help legacy and modern platforms work together during replatforming.

* Experiences that meet quality, performance, and accessibility expectations at scale.

* Visible improvements that reach members while helping the team modernise the platform.

**Student Worker, Brick Technology (role 2)**

As our Student Worker - Frontend Engineer, you'll work in the Digital Element Design area, helping migrate web applications to the LEGO® design system. You'll refactor and replace user interface components, apply design tokens and styles, and help ensure the applications remain responsive and accessible. Working in a TypeScript and React monorepo, you'll contribute to modernising the design ecosystem one component at a time while collaborating closely with designers and engineers.

**Required Qualifications**

* Studying Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related field

* Exposure to or experience with React, TypeScript, and CSS through university, personal, or other projects

* Fluent English

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Applied basic unit testing practices and validated changes using existing test suites

* Explored web accessibility and responsive design principles through projects or coursework

**What you'll build**

* Migrate web applications to the LEGO design system

* Refactor and replace existing user interface components

* Apply design tokens and styling standards across applications

* Help ensure a responsive and accessible user experience

* Contribute to the modernisation of a shared frontend ecosystem used across the team

**Student Worker, Cybersecurity Platforms (role 3)**

As our Student Worker, Software Engineer, Cybersecurity, you'll work across a wide range of cybersecurity platforms, applications, and engineering challenges. You'll help implement software features, build infrastructure through code, and support large-scale security logging solutions. Some of the tools and platforms you'll work with are bought and maintained, while others are built from scratch by the team. You won't be expected to know everything from day one. Instead, you'll learn alongside experienced engineers while contributing to meaningful work from week one.

**Required Qualifications**

* Currently pursuing studies in computer science or a related field

* Exposure to software development through university projects, hobby projects, internships, or similar practical experience

* Fluent English

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience with C# or Next.js

**What you'll build**

* Implement new features across cybersecurity platforms and applications

* Help build and maintain infrastructure through code

* Support the operation of large security logging solutions

* Contribute to both internally developed and vendor-supported security technologies

* Learn new technologies and engineering approaches while supporting the team

**Student Worker, Manufacturing Technology (role 4)**

As our Student Worker, you'll join the Warehousing and Site Logistics product team within Manufacturing Technology. You'll help build and support software solutions used in warehouses, logistics operations, and material handling across manufacturing sites. You'll contribute as a regular member of the team while learning both technical and business-domain topics. The role offers the chance to work on systems with real operational impact, where reliable software helps keep production moving every day.

**Required Qualifications**

* Exposure to or experience working with Typescript, React, and Go

* Fluent English

* Studying computer science, software engineering, or related subject

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Exposure to or experience with Python

**What you'll build**

* Support software solutions used in warehousing, logistics, and material-handling operations

* Contribute to development activities that support factories and warehouses globally

* Work alongside experienced engineers on technology decisions and software delivery

* Help improve systems that support continuous movement of products through the supply chain

* Contribute to initiatives connected to factory expansion and new-site implementation projects

**We're looking for students who**

* Are currently enrolled in Denmark in a **Bachelor’s, Master’s, or Erhvervsakademi** (professional academy) program in fields related to data.

* Preferably graduating summer 2028 or beyond, having at least 1.5-2 years left of studies

* Are curious and willing to learn, with a **positive, team-player attitude**.

* Can be present 15–20 hours per week, ideally with 1–2 days at our **LEGO office in Billund**.

* Are passionate about digital technology and eager to contribute to real projects.

If you're interested in joining us, please prepare your CV and cover letter in English. We also ask that you in your CV or cover letter indicate which role you’re most interested in.

The application portal will remain open from 14th September to 12th October 2026, but it may be taken down earlier so we urge you to apply as soon as possible. If you are shortlisted, you will be invited to attend our Assessment Day on 4th November 2026 at our Kornmarken Campus in Billund. Following the Assessment Day, there will be one final interview round. The expected start date for successful candidates is either 1st December 2026 or 1st January 2027.

#LI-MF2

Applications are reviewed on an ongoing basis. However, please note we do amend or withdraw our jobs and reserve the right to do so at any time, including prior to any advertised closing date. So, if you're interested in this role we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

**What’s in it for you?**

Here is what you can expect:

**Family Care Leave** - We offer enhanced paid leave options for those important times.

**Insurances** – All colleagues are covered by our life and disability insurance which provides protection and peace of mind.

**Wellbeing** - We want our people to feel well and thrive. We offer resources and benefits to nurture physical and mental wellbeing along with opportunities to build community and inspire creativity.

**Colleague Discount** – We know you'll love to build, so from day 1 you will qualify for our generous colleague discount.

**Bonus** - We do our best work to succeed together. When goals are reached and if eligible, you'll be rewarded through our bonus scheme.

**Workplace** - When you join the team you'll be assigned a primary workplace location i.e. one of our Offices, stores or factories. Our hybrid work policy means an average of 3 days per week in the office. The hiring team will discuss the policy and role eligibility with you during the recruitment process.

Children are our role models. Their curiosity, creativity and imagination inspire everything we do. We strive to create a diverse, dynamic and inclusive culture of play at the LEGO Group, where everyone feels safe, valued and they belong.

The LEGO Group is highly committed to equal employment opportunity and equal pay and seeks to encourage applicants from all backgrounds (eg. sex, gender identity or expression, race/ethnicity, national origin, sexual orientation, disability, age and religion) to apply for roles in our team.

The LEGO Group is fully committed to Children’s Rights and Child Wellbeing across the globe. Candidates offered positions with high engagement with children are required to take part in Child Safeguarding Background Screening, as a condition of the offer.

Thank you for sharing our global commitment to Children’s Rights.

Just imagine building your dream career.

Then make it real.

**Join the LEGO® team today.**
